title: Partial run of an emission chain
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet on input $x$, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $e$ map the indices $0,\ldots,|w|$ to states of $M$. Suppose that from every state $e(i)$, for every scanned input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition is the emission action for $w$ at index $i$. If a configuration $c$ is in state $e(0)$, then for every $t\le |w|$, after $t$ steps the machine is in state $e(t)$ and its output is the output of $c$ followed by the first $t$ symbols of $w$.
hypotheses_covered: Machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet and input $x$
Transition agrees with the specified emission action for all scanned symbols and tape symbols
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean
alphabet running on some input $x$, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $e$ be
a map from $\{0,\dots,\abs{w}\}$ into the states of $M$ such that from each
state $e(i)$, regardless of the symbols read, the transition of $M$ is the
emission action for $w$ at index $i$: while $i < \abs{w}$ it appends the
$i$-th symbol of $w$ to the output and passes to $e(i+1)$, and at
$i = \abs{w}$ it halts, in both cases leaving the input head and all work
tapes fixed.  If a configuration $c$ is in state $e(0)$, then for every
$t \le \abs{w}$, after $t$ steps from $c$ the machine is in state $e(t)$ and
its output is the output of $c$ followed by the first $t$ symbols of $w$.
